subject: Business Models
title: When to Innovate Your Model
description: Learn When to Innovate Your Model in one minute.

hook.text: Kodak invented the digital camera in 1975 but kept selling film. It filed for bankruptcy in 2012.

buildup.text: Companies innovate their model when existing revenue streams face disruption from technology or competitors.

discovery.text: The best time to innovate is before you must. Adobe switched to subscriptions while still profitable from licenses.

twist.text: Adobe's stock dropped 17% when it announced subscriptions. Three years later it had tripled in value.

climax.text: Model innovation requires cannibalizing your current business. Most companies wait too long—until it's too late.

punchline.text: Kodak waited, died. Adobe didn't, tripled. Timing is everything.

quiz.question: What happened to Adobe's stock after announcing a subscription model?

details.summary: Companies should innovate their business model when customer acquisition costs rise unsustainably, margins compress under competitive pressure, technology shifts enable new delivery methods, or customer values change. Waiting for crisis makes transformation harder and riskier.
details.whyItMatters: Most companies wait too long to innovate their model, changing only when forced by crisis. Proactive model innovation during profitable periods gives companies the resources and time to experiment without existential pressure.
takeaways: Rising acquisition costs and compressing margins signal model exhaustion
Technology shifts and changing customer values create innovation windows
Proactive innovation during profitable periods is safer than crisis-driven change

faq.question: What are the warning signs that a business model needs innovation?
faq.answer: Declining customer lifetime value, rising acquisition costs, margin compression, new competitors with different models gaining share, technology changes enabling alternatives, regulatory shifts threatening the model, and customer complaints about fundamental value delivery.

faq.question: How can companies experiment with new models without abandoning the current one?
faq.answer: Create separate teams or subsidiaries to test new models. Run pilots with limited customer segments. Use the current business to fund experimentation. Set clear metrics for when to scale or kill experiments. Maintain both models in parallel during transition.
